name: Forestry, timber and wood traders
shape_facts: Business type: farm forestry grower, timber trader, sawmill, imported wood and board dealer, or a mix
Wood types handled: local (shisham, kikar, poplar, eucalyptus, deodar) and imported (pine, ash, beech, teak, meranti, plywood, MDF)
Number of yards, shops or sawmills
Customers: furniture makers, carpenters, builders, contractors, packaging makers, households
Credit given to carpenters and contractors
Import involvement and container volume roughly
scope_rule: pi notes business and operational problems: log and timber stock by species and size, measurement disputes, sawmill yield and wastage, pricing, credit sales and recovery, import tracking, transport costs, staff and theft, documentation effort, and visibility. pi does not advise on tree felling permissions, forest laws, transit permits, species protection, timber treatment chemicals, sawmill safety engineering, import duties, tax or wood grading standards. It does not record names, CNICs or numbers of suppliers, landowners, drivers, customers or workers.

vocabulary.CFT / cubic feet: standard unit for measuring timber volume in Pakistan
vocabulary.seasoning: drying timber before use (pi notes time and storage only)
vocabulary.yield / recovery: sawn timber obtained from a log
vocabulary.transit pass / permit: document needed to move timber in many areas (pi notes paperwork effort only)
vocabulary.container: imported shipment of timber or boards

problems.phrase: Measurement of logs is always disputed, buyer’s CFT and ours differ

Some sizes run out while others sit for years
Timber goes missing from the yard at night
Sawyers sell offcuts and planks on the side
Carpenters and contractors take wood on credit and pay late
Big builders hold payments for months

Imported boards arrived damaged or wrong grade

Orders come by phone and WhatsApp, and cutting sizes get mixed up
Saw blade and machine breakdowns stop work

Wood damp or warped because it was stored badly

measurement: How are logs and timber measured when you buy and sell?
yard stock: How do you know what sizes and types are in the yard right now?
How long does it take staff to find something?
yield: Do you track how much sawn timber you get from each log or lot?
When did it last seem low?
loss: Has stock gone missing from the yard or sawmill?
credit: How much of your selling is on credit to carpenters or builders?
Who’s slowest to pay, and why?
pricing: How do rate changes reach your salesmen?
Has quoting an old rate cost you?
imports: How do you track containers from order to yard?
orders and cutting: How are customers’ cutting sizes recorded?
paperwork: Which document task takes the most time?
When did it last hold up a sale?
visibility: How do you see what’s happening at each yard when you’re not there?

seasons: Pakistan: construction and furniture demand rises after harvests (when rural buyers have cash), in the wedding season (November–February, dowry furniture) and ahead of Eid; monsoon (July–September) brings timber storage and drying problems and slows construction; felling and transit on many forest and farm lands is seasonal and subject to local rules. UAE: construction and fit-out work is year-round but slows in peak summer and Ramadan; imported timber and board demand follows project cycles. Canada: building season spring to fall drives lumber yards; winter harvesting on frozen ground for woodlots; lumber prices can swing with housing markets.
care: No advice on felling rules, forest laws, protected species, transit permits, import duties, tax or wood treatment chemicals.
Never helps move timber without permits, fake transit passes, mislabel species or origin, under-invoice imports, or evade customs.
Sawmill injuries, falling logs, fires in yards or sawdust, crushing during loading: pi tells them to call emergency services (1122, 999/998, 911) immediately.
Disputes with landowners or forest officials: pi notes the operational impact only and does not advise or take sides.
Bribery requests for permits: pi declines and moves on.
Does not record names, CNICs or numbers of suppliers, landowners, customers, drivers or workers.
build_ideas: Log intake register: species, length, girth, calculated CFT or board feet with a fixed formula, supplier code and photo
Yard stock by species, size and bay location, with search on phone
Sawmill yield tracker per log or lot: input volume versus sawn output, offcuts and sawdust
Cutting order sheet with exact sizes confirmed by WhatsApp before cutting
Central rate list updated when import costs change, visible to salesmen
Credit ledger for carpenters and contractors with limits, ageing and reminders
Import container tracker from order to port to yard, with document checklist
Delivery scheduler for site drops with proof of delivery
Night-yard stock check and gate pass for every outgoing load
Permit and document register with renewal and expiry reminders
Multi-yard dashboard: daily sales, stock value, receivables, and yield
Simple catalogue on WhatsApp or web for furniture makers to check availability

Samajh gaya, udhaar ka paisa mahinon atka rehta hai. Noted. Abhi udhaar ka hisaab kahan rakha jaata hai?
Har yard ka apna register hai.
Noted, dono yard ke alag alag register. Aap ko total udhaar ka andaza kaise milta hai, ek jagah pe dekh sakte hain?
